title: Runtime Architecture: Google Provider Restart-Refresh Continuity

components.name: Operator
components.responsibility: Start Google Drive provider connection from the local SPA, complete Google consent in the browser, and rely on daemon-authored connection truth after reconnect or daemon restart.
components.process_boundary: Human interaction with Bot SPA and Google consent UI; never a token custody or ConnectionRegistry writer.
components.authority_role: Sole human consent authority for Google OAuth; not ConnectionRegistry, keyring, or Cloud app-config authority.
outputs: operator expectation that Drive remains usable after daemon restart
components.multiplicity: One human operator per local daemon product home.
prohibited_authority: Author ConnectionRegistry connected without daemon durable secret write
Inject production Google user tokens into Cloud
Treat hosted Supabase Continue with Google as Drive provider auth
Treat pairing session_token as Google OAuth grant

components.name: Cloud Google provider-app-config publisher
components.responsibility: Publish the non-secret GoogleNativeAppConfigV1 payload at GET /api/v1/provider-app-config/google for the active Bicameral environment, including rotation and disablement.
components.process_boundary: Cloud HTTPS route and deploy-time BICAMERAL_GOOGLE_OAUTH_* settings only.
components.deployment_location: Hosted Cloud origin (app/staging); Enforced producer requires main + live HTTP 200.
components.authority_role: Sole authority for Bicameral Google OAuth application identity/configuration; never user-token or ConnectionRegistry authority.
inputs: deploy-provisioned BICAMERAL_GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and related non-secret settings
components.multiplicity: One active published config per Cloud environment.
prohibited_authority: Mint receive persist refresh or interpret user Google access or refresh tokens
Accept authorization codes or PKCE verifiers
Author ConnectionRegistry connected or action_needed
Require Cloud as proxy for normal Drive API calls
Serve hosted Supabase Continue with Google as this hop
Include the Desktop client credential in this route's payload

components.name: Cloud Google Desktop client-credential distributor (amendment, bot#1211 / cloud#309)
components.responsibility: Serve the provider-required Google Desktop client credential only to requests authenticated with the signed-in operator's transient Cloud bearer (presented by the local daemon for this fetch), distinct from and never merged into the public GoogleNativeAppConfigV1 route.
components.process_boundary: Cloud authenticated HTTPS route, gated by the signed-in operator's existing transient Cloud bearer handed to the local daemon for this credential fetch and then discarded; orthogonal to row-12 pairing / daemon-identity enrollment; separate handler and response schema from ELM-CLOUD-APP-CONFIG.
components.deployment_location: Hosted Cloud origin (app/staging); requires signed-in operator Cloud bearer presented by the local daemon (not row-12 daemon-identity enrollment).
components.authority_role: Sole authority for distributing the Desktop client credential value; never Connection truth, never user-token authority, never merged with app-config authority.
inputs: signed-in operator transient Cloud bearer (handed to local daemon for this credential fetch, then discarded; does not require row-12 enrollment)

config_version binding to the credential's owning client_id
outputs: GoogleClientCredentialEnvelopeV1 JSON (credential + bound client_id + config_version), authenticated responses only
explicit rotation/version-mismatch signal, never silent substitution
components.multiplicity: One active credential per Cloud environment, bound to the app-config client_id for that environment.
prohibited_authority: Publish the credential through the unauthenticated app-config route or any other public surface
Accept or store Google authorization codes, PKCE verifiers, or user access/refresh tokens
Author ConnectionRegistry connected or action_needed
Silently serve a rotated credential without a distinguishable version signal

components.name: Local daemon connection gateway
components.responsibility: Resolve Cloud-first Google app config for new OAuth, resolve the Desktop client credential via the authenticated credential-distribution boundary, run PKCE/loopback Google OAuth including the credential on exchange, persist OAuthTokenEnvelopeV1 and GoogleClientCredentialEnvelopeV1 before ConnectionRegistry connected, project credential-backed status, and refresh existing grants (token and client-credential) after real process restart.
components.process_boundary: Local bicameral-gateway connection routes and Google app-config resolver.
components.deployment_location: Operator workstation loopback daemon OS process.
components.authority_role: Sole authority for user Google token custody, refresh, ConnectionCompletionOutcome, and ConnectionRegistry truth.
inputs: explicit opt-in legacy BICAMERAL_GOOGLE_CLIENT_* for interim lab only
cached GoogleClientCredentialEnvelopeV1 from OS keyring, used only when its bound client_id/config_version still matches (amendment)
outputs: durable keyring write (token envelope and, when required, client-credential envelope) then registry connected
credential-backed action_needed projection (missing token or missing/mismatched client credential)
components.multiplicity: One active daemon OS process identity per operator product home.
prohibited_authority: Mark connected before durable secret write succeeds
Silently fall back to in-memory secrets in production
Require live Cloud GET to refresh an existing envelope-recorded grant

Treat presence of the client credential as proof of confidential-client status or a reason to skip PKCE (amendment)

components.name: OS keyring OAuth token and client-credential envelope store
components.responsibility: Durably store OAuthTokenEnvelopeV1 (access, refresh, expires_at, non-secret client_id) and GoogleClientCredentialEnvelopeV1 (Desktop client credential, bound client_id, bound config_version) across real daemon OS process death.
components.process_boundary: OS credential store accessed through OsKeyringSecretsStore only in production.
components.deployment_location: Operator OS keyring (macOS Keychain / Windows Credential Manager / Linux Secret Service).
components.authority_role: Persistence owner for Google user token envelopes and the Desktop client-credential envelope; writers remain the daemon gateway.
components.multiplicity: One envelope record per connection.google oauth_token key; one envelope record per connection.google client_secret key.
prohibited_authority: Silent fallback to volatile in-memory storage in production
Expose envelope contents through ConnectionCompletionOutcome
Store pairing session_token or enrollment grants
Replicate user tokens into Cloud
Replicate the client credential into Cloud (amendment)

components.name: ConnectionRegistry metadata file
components.responsibility: Persist non-secret connection metadata such as status, account_label, capabilities, auth_method, and updated_at under ~/.bicameral/connections.yaml.
components.process_boundary: Daemon-owned local YAML registry file; never secret storage.
components.authority_role: Persistence owner for non-secret connection metadata; connected may be written only after durable envelope write.
inputs: daemon upsert after successful durable secret write
daemon updates on reconnect or revoke paths
components.multiplicity: One metadata row per provider connection id.
prohibited_authority: Store access_token refresh_token or PKCE material
Manufacture effective connected without readable usable credential
Act as Google app-config authority
Share storage with pairing_id relationships

components.name: Google Drive API transport and refresh
components.responsibility: Refresh near-expiry or expired access tokens using the envelope refresh_token plus envelope-recorded non-secret client_id and, when the provider requires it, the keyring-cached Desktop client credential, re-persist the rotated envelope(s), and perform Drive API calls.
components.process_boundary: Daemon-local Drive transport within the gateway/runtime process.
components.deployment_location: Inside the local daemon OS process.
components.authority_role: Executor of refresh and Drive I/O; not ConnectionRegistry writer for initial connected and not Cloud app-config publisher.
inputs: GoogleClientCredentialEnvelopeV1 from OS keyring, when the cached client_id/config_version still matches (amendment)
outputs: refresh failures that force action_needed / re-auth (including missing/mismatched client credential, amendment)
components.multiplicity: One transport path per daemon using the google connection envelope.
prohibited_authority: Require live Cloud GET to refresh an existing grant that already records client_id
Send user tokens to Cloud
Treat stub InMemorySecretsStore restart tests as real process-kill evidence
Use a mismatched or expired client-credential envelope instead of failing to action_needed (amendment)

components.name: Bot SPA connection courier
components.responsibility: Present connect UI and talk only to local daemon connection APIs; never call Cloud provider-app-config and never handle Google user tokens.
components.process_boundary: Bot dashboard SPA running in the operator browser against the local daemon.
components.deployment_location: Operator browser against local daemon origin.
components.authority_role: UI courier only; never ConnectionRegistry, keyring, or Cloud app-config authority.
outputs: connect/start and status requests to daemon
components.multiplicity: Zero or more browser tabs; none holds Google user token authority.
prohibited_authority: GET Cloud /api/v1/provider-app-config/google directly for this hop
Persist or display Google access or refresh tokens
Author connected in ConnectionRegistry
Couple Google OAuth to pairing_id approve semantics

components.name: Google OAuth and Drive IdP/API
components.responsibility: External identity provider and Drive API that issues authorization codes and tokens and serves Drive resources for the granted scopes.
components.process_boundary: Google-hosted OAuth and Drive endpoints outside Bicameral process boundaries.
components.authority_role: External token issuer and Drive resource authority; not Bicameral ConnectionRegistry authority.
inputs: authorization requests with Cloud-published or envelope-recorded client_id
Drive API calls with access token
components.multiplicity: One external Google tenant/app registration consumed per Bicameral environment client_id.
prohibited_authority: Write Bicameral ConnectionRegistry
Publish Bicameral Cloud app-config
Authorize pairing session_token mint

relationships.interaction: Operator starts or inspects Google Drive connection through the SPA.
relationships.handoff: Operator intent becomes daemon connection API calls via the SPA courier.
authority_boundaries: SPA never becomes token custody.
Operator consent does not itself write ConnectionRegistry.

relationships.interaction: SPA calls only local daemon connection start/status/callback-completion surfaces.
authority_boundaries: SPA must not call Cloud provider-app-config for this hop.
Outcomes never include tokens or codes.

relationships.interaction: New OAuth bootstrap fetches non-secret GoogleNativeAppConfigV1 Cloud-first.
relationships.handoff: Daemon validates V1 payload; rejected config never mutates ConnectionRegistry.
authority_boundaries: Cloud returns only non-secret app config.
No user tokens codes or PKCE material cross this relationship.
Existing-grant refresh may skip this GET when envelope client_id is present.
The Desktop client credential never travels this relationship (amendment).

relationships.interaction: Daemon fetches the Desktop client credential from the authenticated distribution boundary when no still-valid matching keyring envelope exists (new OAuth, or cached envelope's client_id/config_version no longer matches), presenting the signed-in operator's transient Cloud bearer for this fetch only.
relationships.medium: Authenticated HTTPS GET using the signed-in operator's transient Cloud bearer (handed to the local daemon, then discarded); distinct route from GET /api/v1/provider-app-config/google; does not require row-12 pairing / daemon-identity enrollment.
relationships.handoff: Daemon persists the returned GoogleClientCredentialEnvelopeV1 to OS keyring; a rejected/failed fetch surfaces as action_needed, never a manufactured credential.
authority_boundaries: This relationship never carries authorization codes, PKCE verifiers, or Google user tokens.
Caller authority is the signed-in operator's transient Cloud bearer only; row 5 remains orthogonal to pairing / daemon-identity enrollment (row 12).
Restart/refresh for an existing grant uses the keyring-cached envelope and does not require this GET unless client_id/config_version has changed.
The credential returned here is provider-required request material, never proof of confidential-client status.

relationships.interaction: Daemon runs PKCE + loopback authorization-code exchange with Google, including the Desktop client credential in the exchange/refresh request when the provider requires it.
relationships.medium: Browser redirect to Google plus loopback callback and token endpoint HTTPS.
relationships.handoff: Daemon receives tokens locally and never forwards them to Cloud.
payloads: authorization URL with client_id scopes state PKCE
token-exchange request: client_id, code, redirect_uri, grant_type, code_verifier, and client_secret when configured (amendment)
authority_boundaries: Code exchange is daemon-local.
Cloud is not an OAuth broker on this path.
PKCE code_verifier is always present regardless of whether client_secret is also sent (amendment).

relationships.interaction: Daemon writes and reads OAuthTokenEnvelopeV1 including non-secret client_id under connection.google/oauth_token, and GoogleClientCredentialEnvelopeV1 under connection.google/client_secret (amendment).
relationships.handoff: Durable envelope(s) must succeed before registry connected; production keyring failure is explicit.
authority_boundaries: Production uses OS keyring only.
No silent in-memory fallback.
InMemorySecretsStore is test-only.

relationships.interaction: Daemon upserts non-secret connection metadata only after durable envelope write on connected paths, and projects action_needed when credentials are missing.
relationships.handoff: Registry metadata and readable credential must agree before effective connected is projected.
authority_boundaries: Registry never stores secrets.
GET projection must not mutate durable registry to invent connected.

relationships.interaction: Drive transport refreshes access tokens and calls Drive APIs.
relationships.medium: HTTPS token endpoint and Drive API.
relationships.handoff: Refresh uses refresh_token + envelope-recorded client_id, plus the keyring-cached client_secret when the provider requires it, for existing grants; success re-persists envelope(s) then continues Drive I/O.
payloads: client_secret when a matching cached envelope exists (amendment)
authority_boundaries: Existing-grant refresh does not require live Cloud GET.
User tokens never enter Cloud.
A missing or mismatched client-credential envelope forces action_needed rather than a refresh attempt without it (amendment).

relationships.interaction: Drive transport loads envelope after restart and re-persists rotated envelope after refresh.
relationships.handoff: Post-restart Drive usability depends on keyring survival across real OS process kill.
authority_boundaries: Envelope client_id is non-secret application identity, not user proof.
Keyring unavailability fails closed.

relationships.interaction: Daemon connection and Drive readiness paths invoke transport refresh/I/O using registry + keyring state.
relationships.handoff: Transport reports readiness or forces re-auth/action_needed on refresh failure.
authority_boundaries: restart-refresh-envelope success requires real process kill continuity, not in-process reconstruction alone.

states.mutation_path: Written only after successful Cloud validation; expired or disabled cache must re-bootstrap and fail closed for new OAuth.
states.lifecycle: Transient helper for new OAuth during temporary Cloud unavailability while expires_at still valid; not Connection truth and not user credential storage.
prohibited_fallbacks: Using expired cache to start new OAuth
Treating cache as proof of user Google authorization

states.artifact: Transient Google OAuth session (PKCE verifier, state, loopback listener)
states.persistence_location: Daemon process memory for the auth session only
states.mutation_path: Created at start; consumed on successful callback/code exchange or terminal failure; not durable across process death as Connection truth.
states.lifecycle: Short-lived until connected, denied, expired, or provider_unavailable.
prohibited_fallbacks: Persisting PKCE verifier into Cloud
Reflecting codes or tokens into the loopback success page
Equating in-flight OAuth with ConnectionRegistry connected

states.mutation_path: Written on successful OAuth before registry connected; rewritten on refresh rotation; must survive real OS process kill.
states.lifecycle: Durable until revoke, refresh failure requiring re-auth, or explicit disconnect.
prohibited_fallbacks: Silent production in-memory envelope storage
Cloud custody of the envelope
Treating InMemorySecretsStore preload as restart-refresh-envelope proof

states.lifecycle: Durable until rotation/mismatch invalidates it, credential-boundary distribution is revoked, or explicit disconnect. Distinct lifecycle from STATE-TOKEN-ENVELOPE: this envelope tracks Bicameral's application identity material, not the operator's Google grant.

Cloud custody in the reverse direction (this store never sends the credential back to Cloud)

Treating this artifact's presence as proof of confidential-client status

states.mutation_path: Upserted only after durable OAuthTokenEnvelopeV1 write succeeds; never authored by Cloud or SPA.
states.lifecycle: Durable metadata across daemon restart; effective projection remains credential-backed.
prohibited_fallbacks: Writing connected before keyring write succeeds
Storing secrets in the registry file
Cloud or SPA forging connected

states.artifact: Drive usable after registry+envelope load and any needed refresh following real daemon restart
states.persistence_location: Derived from surviving OS keyring envelope + registry metadata + successful refresh/Drive I/O
states.mutation_path: After real OS process kill and new daemon process, load envelope+registry, refresh via envelope client_id if needed, then succeed Drive I/O.

prohibited_fallbacks: Counting in-process InMemorySecretsStore reconstruction as readiness proof
Requiring live Cloud GET for existing-grant refresh
Equating pairing reattach with Drive readiness

transitions.trigger: Daemon Cloud-first GET of provider-app-config/google for new OAuth bootstrap validates GoogleNativeAppConfigV1.
transitions.persistence_effect: May also write STATE-APP-CONFIG-CACHE bounded by expires_at; never writes user tokens or ConnectionRegistry connected.

transitions.trigger: Operator starts Google connect; daemon creates PKCE/state and opens Google authorization using Cloud-published client_id.
transitions.persistence_effect: Creates transient auth session only; ConnectionRegistry unchanged.

transitions.trigger: Daemon completes local code exchange and durably writes OAuthTokenEnvelopeV1 including non-secret client_id to OS keyring.
transitions.persistence_effect: Keyring write must succeed; failure fails closed before any connected registry upsert.

transitions.trigger: After durable envelope write succeeds, daemon upserts ConnectionRegistry status=connected metadata.
transitions.persistence_effect: Writes non-secret metadata only; connected is illegal without prior durable secret write.

transitions.trigger: GET /connections or start path finds registry connected without readable usable envelope.
transitions.persistence_effect: Projection only; GET must not mutate durable registry to invent or clear connected.

transitions.trigger: Real OS process kill ends the daemon; a new daemon process starts and reloads OS keyring envelope plus ConnectionRegistry metadata.
transitions.persistence_effect: No new OAuth required when envelope and registry survive; in-process InMemory reconstruction alone is non-conformant for restart-refresh-envelope.

transitions.trigger: After restart or near expiry, Drive transport refreshes using refresh_token + envelope-recorded client_id without live Cloud GET.
transitions.persistence_effect: Re-persists rotated OAuthTokenEnvelopeV1 retaining client_id for subsequent restarts.

transitions.trigger: Credential-backed connected path completes any needed refresh and succeeds Drive I/O after real process restart.
transitions.persistence_effect: Observes restart-refresh-envelope topology fact: new daemon process + keyring + registry keep Drive usable.

scenarios.name: New Google OAuth is Cloud-first app-config then local PKCE
scenarios.trigger: Operator connects Google Drive with no usable existing grant.
authority_boundaries: New OAuth requires Cloud-first GET /api/v1/provider-app-config/google (or still-valid cache); legacy BICAMERAL_GOOGLE_CLIENT_* only with explicit opt-in for interim lab notes.
Cloud never receives user tokens.
connected only after durable keyring write.
scenarios.expected_result: OS keyring holds OAuthTokenEnvelopeV1 with client_id and ConnectionRegistry is connected.
scenarios.failure_behavior: Missing/malformed/disabled/expired app-config or keyring write failure fails closed without connected.

scenarios.name: Real OS process kill then Drive still usable
scenarios.trigger: Operator or harness kills the daemon OS process and starts a new daemon process after a completed Google connection.
authority_boundaries: Passing restart-refresh-envelope means real OS process kill → new daemon process → Drive still usable from OS keyring + ConnectionRegistry.
In-process InMemorySecretsStore reconstruction alone is insufficient evidence.
scenarios.expected_result: New daemon process loads envelope + registry, refreshes if needed, and Drive remains usable without new OAuth.
scenarios.failure_behavior: Missing keyring continuity, refresh failure, or registry/credential disagreement yields action_needed / re-auth rather than false connected.

scenarios.name: Existing grant refreshes from envelope client_id without live Cloud GET
scenarios.trigger: Access token near expiry or expired after restart while envelope still holds refresh_token and client_id.
authority_boundaries: Existing-grant refresh may use envelope-recorded non-secret client_id without live Cloud GET.
New OAuth remains Cloud-first and is out of this scenario's refresh path.
scenarios.expected_result: Rotated envelope is re-persisted and Drive I/O succeeds without contacting provider-app-config.
scenarios.failure_behavior: Refresh error or missing client_id/refresh_token fails closed into re-auth / action_needed.

scenarios.name: Cloud never holds user Google tokens
scenarios.trigger: Any new OAuth, refresh, or restart continuity path executes.
authority_boundaries: Cloud publishes only non-secret app config.
User Google tokens remain daemon/OS-keyring local.
Hosted Supabase Continue with Google is out of scope for this hop.
scenarios.expected_result: No user Google access_token, refresh_token, authorization code, or PKCE verifier is accepted or stored by Cloud.
scenarios.failure_behavior: Any Cloud user-token custody path is a cut-point invariant failure for this contract.

scenarios.name: OAuth/Drive continuity is orthogonal to pairing

scenarios.expected_result: Google envelope and ConnectionRegistry continuity do not require or mint pairing_id; pairing session_token does not author Drive connected.

scenarios.name: Legacy BICAMERAL_GOOGLE_CLIENT_* is explicit opt-in lab only

scenarios.expected_result: Without explicit opt-in, missing Cloud config fails closed rather than silently using legacy env as production authority.

scenarios.name: Production secrets are OS keyring only
scenarios.trigger: Daemon persists or reloads Google OAuth secrets in production topology.
authority_boundaries: Production SecretsStore is OsKeyringSecretsStore only.
Keyring unavailability is an explicit failure.
InMemorySecretsStore remains test-only.
scenarios.expected_result: Envelope survives only via OS keyring across real process death; no silent in-memory production fallback.
scenarios.failure_behavior: Keyring failure blocks connected and cannot be papered over with volatile memory.
